title: OpenAI refers Darren Zhou’s threats to the FBI; local police investigate and he pleads guilty to stalking and threat charges
summary: Through the FBI, OpenAI disclosed threats that Darren Zhou wrote in ChatGPT against his ex-girlfriend, and he later pleaded guilty to stalking and threat charges.
account: Darren Zhou wrote threats against his ex-girlfriend in ChatGPT. Court reporting describes an OpenAI emergency disclosure that reached the Palm Beach County Sheriff’s Office through the FBI. According to the probable cause affidavit cited by the Sun Sentinel, the FBI told the sheriff's office about the messages six days before the arrest. Deputies compared those messages with anonymous threats that the ex-girlfriend had preserved. The woman told detectives that she had not reported Zhou to police because she did not want to cause his behavior to escalate. The sheriff’s booking entry lists 29 May 2026 as his arrest date. BocaNewsNow reports that he pleaded guilty on 13 August 2026 to written threats, aggravated stalking, and unlawful use of a two-way communication device. Adjudication was withheld, and he received eight years of probation, two years of GPS monitoring, and restrictions on contact and weapons. The reporting cites court documents, and it does not reproduce the complete affidavit or plea order. It supports a police intervention and court restrictions. No source shows that an attack would otherwise have occurred.
purpose: OpenAI says that when it detects users planning to harm others, it routes the conversations to a small team trained on its usage policies. It says that if human reviewers find an imminent threat of serious physical harm to others, it may refer the case to law enforcement. This referral is that designed use. ChatGPT itself is a general-purpose assistant, which Zhou used to rehearse his plans.
system: ChatGPT (OpenAI), with OpenAI's automated detection and human review pipeline for users planning to harm others
domain: Public safety - stalking and threat investigation
segment: Consumer chatbot trust-and-safety referral to law enforcement

fields.summary: Through the FBI, OpenAI disclosed threats that Darren Zhou wrote in ChatGPT against his ex-girlfriend, and he later pleaded guilty to stalking and threat charges.
fields.account: Darren Zhou wrote threats against his ex-girlfriend in ChatGPT. Court reporting describes an OpenAI emergency disclosure that reached the Palm Beach County Sheriff’s Office through the FBI. According to the probable cause affidavit cited by the Sun Sentinel, the FBI told the sheriff's office about the messages six days before the arrest. Deputies compared those messages with anonymous threats that the ex-girlfriend had preserved. The woman told detectives that she had not reported Zhou to police because she did not want to cause his behavior to escalate. The sheriff’s booking entry lists 29 May 2026 as his arrest date. BocaNewsNow reports that he pleaded guilty on 13 August 2026 to written threats, aggravated stalking, and unlawful use of a two-way communication device. Adjudication was withheld, and he received eight years of probation, two years of GPS monitoring, and restrictions on contact and weapons. The reporting cites court documents, and it does not reproduce the complete affidavit or plea order. It supports a police intervention and court restrictions. No source shows that an attack would otherwise have occurred.
